payload.summary: Planned the drift-gate attribution rework (items 4-7 of the original seven-item request) after archiving the prerequisites that blocked its spec deltas. Planning verified three defects beyond the original scope, the sharpest being that the same tree yields CI success and local exit 2 -- a violation of the ratified 'Gate reproduces locally' scenario. Those three are in scope, because attribution layered on an environment-dependent base inherits the ambiguity.

decisions.title: Base reference resolves to one recorded revision, preferring the remote ref
decisions.rationale: Verified on a branch byte-identical to origin/main: --base main exits 2 while --base origin/main exits 0, because _default_changed_files (gate.py:359) diffs the local ref while describe_tree (gate.py:735) compares against origin/<base>. The remote ref wins because CI's fresh checkout already effectively uses it; preferring local would make CI the outlier and leave the split unfixed.

decisions.title: Attribution uses path-level ancestry rather than content fingerprints
decisions.rationale: compute_input_fingerprint reads working-tree bytes only and takes no revision; making it revision-aware would change the hashed payload format and invalidate every recorded input_fingerprint. Path-level comparison is a sound over-approximation because attribution is coarser than freshness, and its only error mode -- a file that changed and changed back reading as inherited -- runs away from blame, which is the safe direction for the failure being fixed.

decisions.title: Attribution is a separate axis, not a fifth classification group
decisions.rationale: classify_degradation must stay pure: TestPurity asserts no IO by patching, and attribution shells out to git. test_classify_degradation.py:235 additionally hard-pins the informational set. Severity and ownership are independent questions and folding them together would conflate them.

decisions.title: Event behaviour lives inside one always-running CI job
decisions.rationale: requirement-traceability-sweep (ci.yml:626, dispatch ci.yml:737-798) already does this and its comment rejects the job-level if: outright -- a required check that does not run on merge_group is not a check on the merge candidate, and a skipped required check reports success to branch protection.

decisions.title: The remediation servo is confined to dependency-update pull requests
decisions.rationale: This is the repository's first contents: write grant and first job-level permissions block; both workflows are contents: read today and GITHUB_TOKEN appears once as a read token. Dependabot is provably never the cause of context drift and produces up to 15 pull requests weekly, so it is both the real pain and the safest population to confine a new write grant to.

decisions.title: Both promotion notes are rewritten in one edit
decisions.rationale: introduce-fitness-function-gates wrote session-completion.md:69-115 immediately below the known-gap section and back-references it, and specs/fitness-functions/spec.md:115-116 makes that adjacency normative. Deleting the known-gap section alone leaves a ratified claim pointing at nothing.

next_steps: wp-base and wp-context-impact can dispatch immediately in parallel; they share no files and neither has dependencies.
wp-base, wp-attribution and wp-events are strictly sequential -- all three write gate.py, and attribution against an unpinned base is meaningless.
Task 7.2 requires the repository owner: a pull request cannot change branch protection.
